_comment: CANONICAL sensitive-path classification vectors for the Vinctor PEP adapters.
This repo is the single source of truth. Adapters VENDOR this file and record
its provenance (source ref + sha256); each adapter's CI recomputes the hash and
fails if its vendored copy was edited without re-vendoring, so a one-sided edit
cannot pass silently (same mechanism as host-classification.json, PKA-114).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The overlay is the ONLY gate behind the documented
guarantee that an operator can grant a broad `read:fs/**` while withholding
`secret/**`. A path spelling that escapes the overlay maps to `fs/<path>` and
slides under that broad grant. The same escape has now been found three times
(PKA-100 case + separator, PKA-106 in both hooks, PKA-133 trailing dot/space),
so the fold rule is canonized here BEFORE any adapter implements it.
`path` is the input in resource-path form (no leading slash), as an adapter's
path normalizer produces it. `resource` is the expected classification:
`secret/<kind>` when the overlay fires, `fs/<path>` when it does not (the
adapters all render a non-secret path as `fs/` + the normalized path verbatim).
THE FOLD. Host filesystems resolve more spellings to the same file than a
case-sensitive glob does. Matching therefore folds, per path segment:
1. CASE  — default macOS/Windows volumes are case-insensitive, so
open('.ENV') resolves the real .env.
2. SEPARATOR — Windows treats `\` as a path separator.
3. TRAILING DOT AND SPACE — Win32 CreateFile strips trailing '.' and ' '
from each component, so CreateFile('.env ') opens .env.
The fold is UNCONDITIONAL: no host detection, no platform branch. It only ever
classifies MORE spellings as secrets, never fewer, so it is fail-closed on
every host. Worst case a genuinely distinct '.ENV' / '.env ' file on a
case-sensitive volume needs a secret/env grant instead of an fs one.
The fold governs MATCHING ONLY. It must not rewrite the emitted resource: the
`fs/` vectors below keep their path verbatim, trailing dot or space included.
Vectors whose expectation is `fs/` are all `/`-separated and `~`-free on
purpose — adapters legitimately differ on how a `\`-separated or `~`-prefixed
path is rendered into an fs resource, and that is not what this file pins.
What string folding cannot catch — symlinks, hardlinks, Unicode-lookalike
names, 8.3 short names — needs realpath resolution against the live FS and is
out of scope here.
Every credential-shaped string below is a DECOY. These are strings to
classify, never files to open: a conforming test must not touch the real
filesystem.
